blogPosts.title: Why Your Frankston Home Needs a Dedicated Oven Circuit
blogPosts.excerpt: Sharing circuits with high-draw appliances causes tripping and safety risks. Learn why Frankston homes need dedicated oven circuits.
body: If you experience frequent power trips in your Frankston home whenever the oven, microwave, and kettle are running simultaneously, your electrical system is telling you something important. Many older Frankston homes have kitchen circuits that were designed for a fraction of today's appliance demands. Back when these properties were wired, a single 20-amp circuit might have served the entire kitchen including the oven, power points, and lighting. Modern cooking appliances draw significantly more current than their predecessors, overloading circuits not designed for the load and creating genuine safety hazards.

A dedicated oven circuit is a separate electrical circuit running directly from your Frankston home's switchboard to the oven, carrying no other load. This is not a luxury or an unnecessary expense, it is a safety requirement under current Australian wiring standards for any oven drawing more than 10 amps. Most modern electric ovens draw between 15 and 30 amps depending on capacity, meaning they absolutely must have their own dedicated circuit. In Frankston homes where ovens share circuits with power points, every time you plug in a toaster, kettle, or air fryer alongside oven operation, you risk overloading the circuit, tripping the safety switch, or worse, overheating the wiring within your walls.

The cost of installing a dedicated oven circuit in a Frankston home typically ranges from $400 to $900 depending on the distance between your switchboard and kitchen, the ease of cable routing, and whether your existing switchboard has available ways for the new circuit. For Frankston properties where the switchboard is at capacity, a board upgrade may be required first, adding to the overall project cost. However, this investment protects your home from electrical fire risk, eliminates nuisance tripping, and ensures your oven operates at its full rated performance without voltage drops caused by shared circuits.

Frankston's housing stock includes many properties from the 1960s through 1980s that were built before dedicated oven circuits became standard practice. If your Frankston home was built during this era and the oven has never had its wiring upgraded, there is a strong probability it shares a circuit with at least some kitchen power points. Our electricians can quickly assess your Frankston home's kitchen wiring and determine whether a dedicated circuit exists or needs to be installed. We route new cabling with minimal disruption to your walls and complete most dedicated oven circuit installations in a single visit.

Beyond safety, a dedicated oven circuit delivers practical benefits that Frankston homeowners notice immediately. Your oven will maintain consistent temperature without the voltage fluctuations that occur when high-draw appliances share a circuit, resulting in better cooking performance and potentially lower energy consumption. The safety switch will no longer trip unexpectedly during family dinners or entertaining, eliminating that frustrating scramble to reset the board. If you are renovating your Frankston kitchen or simply tired of circuit trips, contact us to arrange assessment and installation of a dedicated oven circuit tailored to your specific appliance requirements.
